title: State of the Feed — Week of August 24–30, 2026
content_html:
The aggregator processed 16,863 articles across 11 runs this week, averaging 80 quality articles per run. News dominated the category breakdown with 275 articles, followed by AI-tech with 166 and wellness with 110. Local, climate, and homelab content each contributed between 48–54 articles, while design and science each yielded 62. Remaining categories (scifi, outdoors, homestead) produced 14–22 articles collectively. The dimensional scoring model weighted relevance at 0.55, quality at 0.25, and local interest at 0.20.

Pipeline efficiency remained stable with a mean noise-to-signal ratio of 1.91 across 19 runs (range 0.56–2.86), indicating consistent filtering performance. Twenty feeds were added this week, including Columbia Journalism Review, Nieman Lab, and Hyperallergic for editorial and design content, alongside technical blogs from Dropbox, Pinterest, and MIT's STS program. Feed health monitoring flagged 5 feeds with persistent errors: Neowin, FolkloreThursday, Small Farm Canada, Harvard Health Blog, and Old House Journal.

Discovery analysis identified three high-scoring candidates for potential subscription: the comments section from an article on regenerative agriculture (87.5), comments on Solarpunk Magazine (81.3), and the Solarpunk Magazine feed itself (75.4).

Calibration

KnobOldNewRationale
limits.min_claude_score2023User feedback threshold_sweep shows current min_claude_score=20 cuts only 30.0% of bad articles while losing 9.0% of good ones—unacceptable given 65.8% overall bad rate. The sweep shows min_claude_score=25 would cut 36.9% of bad at 11.7% good lost. Final feed sizes are 462–807/run (mean 626 across last 5 runs), well above the ~100 target, confirming substantial capacity to tighten. The dimensional scoring rearchitecture has stabilized (noise-to-signal at 0.56–0.88 recent runs), so this is the right time to raise quality floors. News category alone has 75.5% bad rate (640/848 rated) yet passes 475 articles through quality gate—the floor is demonstrably too low. Band_precision shows even 40-59 composite scores are 52.7% bad, proving the gate must be stricter. Raising to 25 is conservative (still 5 points below max_step=30) but addresses user-verified quality crisis.
